questions.q: How does the chapter describe fear of silence?
options: As a sign of weak faith
As common, not a sign of weak faith, and something with practical ways to work with it
As rare and unusual
As spiritual opposition to be resisted
questions.explanation: The silence is always adjustable: shorten it, open your eyes, move, add neutral sound, contact support, or stop.

questions.q: What does Job 2:13 show about silence?
options: Silence as punishment
Silence as companionship: Job's friends sat with him seven days without a word
Silence as a technique to hear God
Silence as a sign of anger
questions.explanation: Their silent presence may have been the closest they came to giving Job what he needed. Their later speeches did far more harm.

questions.q: What is the silence this retreat asks for?
options: Emptying the mind of all thought
Attention: putting down other noise to attend to one thing, a line of Scripture or a phrase of prayer, and to the God it points to
Complete soundlessness in a soundproof room
Thirty minutes minimum, no exceptions
questions.explanation: You are not trying to become blank but present to God, who is already present to you. Background sound may remain; the boundary is about deliberate input.

questions.q: Which of the three forms of silence is described as best for anxiety, trauma sensitivity, or accessibility needs?
options: Still silence
Moving silence
Supported silence: eyes open, neutral sound, a trusted person nearby
None; such readers should skip silence
questions.explanation: None of the three is more spiritual than the others. Adaptation is not avoidance when it makes attention more accessible.

options: A heavy object to hold
Something you return to when attention drifts, ideally a short line of Scripture from the session's passage
A person who watches you
A fixed thirty-minute timer
questions.explanation: Say your line slowly when you notice you have wandered, then let it go again. Breath, feet on the floor, a textured object or an open-eyed focus can also serve.

questions.q: How does the chapter distinguish ordinary discomfort from distress?
options: There is no difference
Discomfort is restlessness or wandering attention you return from; distress is panic, a racing heart that will not settle, or feeling back in a memory, and it means stop
Distress is what makes silence work
Discomfort is a sign to stop immediately
questions.explanation: Stop the silence, open your eyes, stand, and use the orientation exercise from Chapter 5. If distress recurs or is severe, do not continue the silent portions alone.

reflection: Which of the fears at the start of this chapter is closest to yours? Write it in a sentence.
What length of silence can you honestly manage right now?
What will your anchor phrase be for the first session?
Still, moving, or supported silence? Eyes open or closed? Decide before you begin, and give yourself permission to change.
